Steamed White Rice for Ullambana Offerings

Served at: Buddhist Ghost Festival (Ullambana)

Serves 4-6 (as an offering)Prep 5 minCook 25 min

During the Buddhist Ghost Festival, also known as Ullambana or Obon, simple and pure food offerings are central to honoring ancestors and providing sustenance to hungry ghosts. Steamed white rice, a fundamental staple in many Asian cultures, symbolizes purity and nourishment, making it a common and essential offering during this time.

Ingredients

  • 2 cups (400g) medium-grain white rice (such as Jasmine or Calrose)
  • 3 cups (720ml) cold water

Method

  1. Rinse the rice: Place the rice in a fine-mesh sieve or a bowl and rinse under cold running water until the water runs clear. This step removes excess starch and helps achieve a fluffier texture.
  2. Combine rice and water: Transfer the rinsed rice to a medium saucepan with a tight-fitting lid. Add the cold water.
  3. Bring to a boil: Place the saucepan over high heat and bring the water to a rolling boil.
  4. Reduce heat and simmer: Once boiling, immediately reduce the heat to the lowest setting, cover the pot tightly with the lid, and simmer for 18-20 minutes, or until all the water has been absorbed. Do not lift the lid during this cooking period.
  5. Rest: Remove the pot from the heat and let it rest, still covered, for another 10 minutes. This allows the steam to redistribute evenly, resulting in perfectly cooked and fluffy rice.
  6. Fluff and serve: Gently fluff the rice with a fork before serving or arranging it in a clean bowl as an offering.

Tips

  • For traditional offerings, present the rice in a small, clean bowl, typically without any adornments or seasonings.
  • Purity is key for offerings; avoid adding salt, butter, or any other flavorings to the rice.
  • While medium-grain rice is common, any preferred type of white rice can be used for this simple preparation.
